title: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”. What was written in times past, in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua and the rest, was written so that we could go back and look upon it. Why? Because we need to learn, and the closer we get to that day, the more we have to learn.

Paul wrote Romans, and Paul lived far after the prophet Isaiah, and after Christ died. He wrote much of the New Testament: Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Colossians, Thessalonians. Yet he tells us to look into the past. So the Christian church that says just deal with the New Testament has it wrong.

Wars are here, right now, and the Most High God and his Son are about war. So we take a journey through past times of war and destruction to prepare our minds for the wars that are here and for the ultimate war to come. We cannot imagine what is coming, but we can hope, and that is our hope.

“sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”: that is us, the twelve tribes of Israel. Isaiah was not talking about the Hittites or anybody else, only the Israelites. A sinful nation is a nation that breaks God’s laws. Laden means drenched and soaked: like a ladle you dip into soup, we are soaked and drenched with iniquity. That’s our people.

“a seed of evildoers”: we are children of evildoers, to the point that we call evil good and call what is good bad. “children that are corrupters”: and our leaders corrupt us. The leaders of this people cause them to err. We are led by Christian pastors, and some of our people by Islam, by leaders who cause us to be corrupt and go astray.

“they have forsaken the Lord”. To turn back to the Lord we have to acknowledge our sins, forsake them and repent as the twelve tribes of Israel. Ask black people in Detroit, Cleveland, Miami, San Francisco, Oakland, New Orleans and New York who they are, what their nationality is, and you get a buffoonery of stupid answers from people who want to sound deep. That shows how much we have been destroyed.

“they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. That is why we went into slavery. From about 1865 to 1965, from the Emancipation Proclamation to the Civil Rights Bill, the racism was more overt, but we had morals and civility: we knew how to treat one another, women had a dress code, and there was an order to how you talked to a sister. We have lost all of that. What have we gained since 1965? Almost twenty million abortions by black women alone, and the dumbest generation of children in the history of the planet, with technology and AI to cheat with.

The whole head is sick. You’re sick, I’m sick, we’re sick. That is why we cannot desire the day of the Lord: we are not right, and we have to keep getting right.

precepts.why:
What is sin? “Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments!” Sin is when we don’t keep God’s commandments. We always go to the epistle of John for that, but precept is upon precept, and this one belongs in the brothers’ arsenal too.

So when Isaiah calls Israel a sinful nation, it is a nation that does not keep God’s commandments, and that is why the woe is upon us.

Who were given God’s commandments? The twelve tribes of Israel. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob”: Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and he later became Israel. “his statutes and his judgments unto Israel”: to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So when modern-day Christians say God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don’t know the Bible. “and as for his judgments, they have not known them”: because the Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why black people went into slavery in the transatlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So the sinful nation of Isaiah 1:4 is us. Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites, the one people given the commandments.

sense.text:
“Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east”: what today they call the Middle East. Ezra saw this way back in his time. That is how you know God has a connection with the Israelites.

There is an order that has to happen. It is not going to be the Iranians getting missiles from China and destroying everything in the US, and the US dropping nukes. This war is not the end. Wars are here and more are coming, and the mindset has to be: I have to get right. Not the Christian church’s I’m saved, brother. We have wicked hearts, and we are rehearsing the righteous acts.

So it makes no sense for those who live near a school to skip the Sabbath, lie, or feign sick because they don’t feel like coming, or to take a job working on the Sabbath when another job could have been found. The Sabbath and the new moons are where we can be in an environment to get right. Staying home means you don’t fear the Lord. Look at what is going on around you and pay attention. If I’m talking about you, I’m talking about you; we are all part of that.

“the nations of the dragons of Arabia” are the Arabs, the sons of Ishmael: the Iraqis, the Syrians, the people of Jordan, in modern times the people of northern Egypt and the top coast of Africa along the Mediterranean, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain and Kuwait. There are some in Australia, England and the United States, but the bulk of them are in that region. Not dragons like Game of Thrones: dragons, meaning they are fierce.

The six Arab monarchies of the Gulf Cooperation Council, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain, are among these nations. They are run by trillionaires and billionaires who are in America’s and Britain’s back pocket, living the lavish life their deals with the US over oil afford them. The people can’t stand those leaders. The 95 percent and more, the citizens, the sons of Ishmael, are mad, and they never wanted the US bases there. In Bahrain, where the Fifth Fleet is headquartered, the Arabs were outside applauding as Iranian missiles flew over their heads to strike the US base. It is happening in Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, Oman and the Emirates too.

“shall come out with many chariots”. If you have chariots you have power, and the Arabs have no power right now. Over 100,000 Palestinian Arabs have been killed, and not even the Saudi crown princes could do anything about it. There is no national Arab army driving ships to the Palestine shore to defend them, because they cannot. It is not time yet in prophecy.

“and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth”: they are going to move together, as one mind. Right now they are divided. Iraq fought Saudi Arabia, there were the Gulf Wars one and two; Esau, through deception, money, the Mossad and the CIA, divided that whole region. But a time is coming when the Arabs unite, and this war is a major part of bringing them together. Iran controls the Strait of Hormuz, only about twenty miles wide, and the Gulf countries depend on it for food and water, and on desalination plants for drinking water. If the food, the water and the oil are cut off, the sons of Ishmael will rise up, because their leaders failed them by getting in bed financially with the United States of America.

“that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” Nobody is afraid of the Arabs right now; the Israelis are not worried about them at all. They are starting to worry about the Iranians, who are bombing Israel right now. But the fear is coming.

We are not pro-Arab and we are not pro-Israeli. We are pro-God, because we are the real Israelites, and all of this is happening because of us. When we come back to the Most High God and his Son, we will be delivered from our enemies and placed back in the land where we deserve to be. We don’t want anybody to die, but rich men make war and poor men fight it.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood”: the Carmanians are the modern-day Iranians. “and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them”. Watch the order: the Arabs lead the charge, and the Carmanians join battle with them. That is not happening right now, and that is how we know this war is not the end.

Iran is not alone. China and Russia stand behind it with intelligence, missiles, technology and even pilots, and it is part of BRICS. It has spent twenty years preparing, hiding missiles in its mountains, and its rockets are breaching the Iron Dome. But Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help to unite the Arabs. The war to come, the third world war, Armageddon in the valley of Megiddo, we don’t know when it will happen, but we can see we are getting closer and closer to that time.

“Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord!” Christians say they are saved, sanctified and filled with the Holy Ghost, and they can’t wait for that day because they turned their life to Jesus. That goes exactly against the prophets and against Christ himself.

You might say you are ready: you wear your fringes, your beard is right, you keep the Sabbath holy and don’t work on it, you don’t eat pork, you don’t have a problem with pornography. But there are other things: patience, anger, a brawling spirit, casting an evil eye. Some of you put the pork down but won’t put the weed down, because it takes the edge off. Now is not the time to roll in that spirit.

We had better not desire the day of the Lord, because we are not right. We are sick, and we have to keep getting right.

“Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the Lord”: “for he hath triumphed gloriously”. “the horse and his rider” is the Egyptian army. Pharaoh hardened his heart and chased the Israelites, and Israel sang gloriously, celebrating and remembering the destruction of the Egyptian army. The Lord is all for the destruction of these nations’ armies.

Everything happening now, God the Father and God the Son love war. When the Israelites were in our righteousness, God fought for us and we destroyed nations. That is a little history and a little faith booster.

“The Lord is my strength and song”: amid everything going on, that is how we as the Israelites get our strength. “and he is become my salvation”: we have to endure to the end keeping the commandments, and through all this craziness, the wars and the wars to come, we trust in the Lord. “he is my God”: he will guide us. That is how we get saved by the Lord: trust in him, endure to the end and do his commandments.

“and I will prepare him an habitation”. The habitation we ultimately want is the kingdom of heaven. A real kingdom is us having power, us ruling, us having servants and handmaids: all the wrongs that were done to us turned upside down, and the right instilled in the earth. Not some pie-in-the-sky fairy tale we learned in modern-day Christianity. “my father’s God, and I will exalt him.”

“The Lord is a man of war”: that is why Israel sang about the destruction of the Egyptian army. God the Father, through his Son Christ, is bringing war. We serve a terrible God, terrible but merciful as well, and he is going to use these nations to bring about a final battle. I pray that I make it, and that you make it, to be part of something we can’t imagine.

precepts.why:
To be guided, many of us choose the ways of the world: our job guides us, our children guide us. We have to search out the fear of the Lord and the kingdom of heaven with fear and trembling. Each of us has to walk a path, and some of us start to go off it. Seek good and not evil.

“My son, forget not my law”: God’s laws. “but let thine heart keep my commandments”: your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, which proves that the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee.” Despite all the wars, rumors of wars and mayhem going on throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said. “Let not mercy and truth forsake thee”.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart”: trust that these prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help to unite the Arabs, and you are seeing that. “and lean not unto thine own understanding.” Some of us in the Christian church used to say we were already saved. That is not the understanding. The understanding is that we must endure to the end, and then the same shall be saved. We don’t know when that end is coming, so we keep enduring, keeping the commandments and doing what we have to do, seeking the good and not the evil.

“In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.” That is how the Lord, our strength and salvation in Moses’ song, is our God who guides us.

sense.text: “His eyes were as a flame of fire, and on his head were many crowns; and he had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.” So what are you tripping about the name for? YHWH, Yahawashi: we learned Jesus Christ in English, and if you want to call him Yahawashi, call him that. What matters is that we keep the commandments.

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood”: because Christ is about righteous destruction. “and his name is called The Word of God.” Jesus Christ will come back, and when he comes back he is not going to meet them as a man. He is coming back to make war.

precepts.why: How do we know this is talking about Jesus? “The Revelation of Jesus Christ”. The whole book is the revelation of Jesus Christ, so the one clothed in a vesture dipped in blood, whose name is called The Word of God, is Jesus the Christ coming back.

“His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire”: the same eyes as a flame of fire that are on the one in Revelation 19. That is how we know it is Jesus Christ.

“And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace”. You can’t deny it anymore: Jesus Christ was a black man. The Bible shows it first and foremost, and there is archaeological proof and historical evidence. Everyone knows it except the Americans in this country, and many of us were those dumb Americans at one point. Many Eastern Europeans know Jesus was black; Vladimir Putin knows Jesus was black.

That is the Christ who is coming back to make war.

sense.text:
“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon”. The United States of America is the daughter of Babylon. Isaiah was speaking prophetically of Babylon the Great to come, the same Babylon John wrote about in Revelation.

“How hath the oppressor ceased!” India, Japan and other nations are aligned with the US, yet they are oppressed by it. India, the most populous country in the world, depends on the Persian Gulf for some 60 percent of its oil, and Japan, one of the world’s largest economies, for 70 percent, and Iran controls what goes in and out of that Gulf. You think our oil prices are high? Wait till you see what happens in Japan and India.

“the golden city ceased!” America is the golden city. Brothers from the islands say they want to get to America because they think money grows on trees. People die on the journey from South America up through Central America to get to this country for opportunity. Nobody is fighting to get into Russia or China. This is the golden city John spoke about in Revelation.
“The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked”: and these people are wicked as hell. “and the sceptre of the rulers.”

“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee”: like saying, I see you, bro. Everyone has seen how powerful the US is, and now they will look narrowly upon it: that’s you? You used to be powerful. “and consider thee, saying”: don’t cross the US, they would say, because they feared it. Now nations are going to say, you’re weakening us, United States. This man is weakening his own allies: Donald Trump is talking about embargoing Spain, a NATO country with trade agreements with 195 countries.

“Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”: this is not ancient Babylon, because John lived way after. This man is the United States of America, and the United States is not run by Arabs or black American men. It is run by Caucasians, the so-called white man. We say white and black because those are the words they gave us: black men didn’t make the water fountain signs that said white. They did all that evil in the Congo and to our brothers and sisters in Africa, many of whom are Israelites. With 845 bases, and sanctions and embargoes on every country that didn’t agree with their policy, they made the earth tremble, starting when they dropped the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki and killed and injured hundreds of thousands. That marked the span of their rule from 1945 until almost now.

“that did shake kingdoms”: he shook kingdoms apart. And God is behind it all, putting it into the hearts of the neocons and war hawks around Donald Trump, hardening his heart to do just what God wants, just as he did with Egypt. How could a country as small as Israel, our homeland, not even as big as Jordan, have that much power over the world’s largest military? Because God is a master. He put the spirit in the Mossad and the CIA to maneuver in politics and funding, buying people out and putting them on the payroll, so that Republican or Democrat, they carry out the will of that man, Netanyahu, and fight wars on his behalf. Candace Owens and Tucker Carlson understand that AIPAC funds both the Republicans and the Democrats, but they can’t do anything to stop it. God set it up so the least of the flock could draw the US out. So when these wars happen, we don’t need to be surprised.

“That made the world as a wilderness”: wherever they go they destroy things, not only physically but spiritually. They are celebrating Christmas in Kuwait, and there are strip clubs in countries that never had them, while they say you’re oppressing the women over there. The Arab women and the women of Iran are happy with their culture. It is not our culture, but they are happy with it. “and destroyed the cities thereof”.

precepts.why:
“And upon her forehead was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS”. John the Revelator lived during the Roman Empire, way after Isaiah. Why would John be talking about ancient Babylon? Isaiah and John were both talking about Babylon the Great to come: the United States of America.

Does that mean Babylon is one big brothel, with the main hoe in the United States pimping out the other hoes? No. It is a similitude. Everybody except the Israelites says no one knows who this is. This is not talking about Iraq. It is talking about the United States of America, and we hope the Lord opens the eyes of our black people, our Hispanic people and the Native Americans who cannot see it.

So the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14 is the United States, weakening all these nations, with God putting it into the hearts of its leaders, just as he did with Egypt.

sense.text:
“And though they go into captivity before their enemies”: the Israelites, the twelve tribes, went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. The Iranians don’t get a pass: they had us in captivity too, just like the princes of Ishmael, whether Amalek or the so-called US.

“thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them”: the sword is the wicked of the time, and the wicked now is the United States. God uses them to bring in all these wars while we have to get right. That is why we went into slavery. Chattel slavery, Jim Crow, the human zoos were real; black men are being hung on college campuses in these last several months, men with great lives ahead of them. That is the judgment of God, a harsh thing to understand, and we have to turn back to him. Slavery is happening right now in parts of Africa, in 2025 and 2026, and it is not black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power.

“and I will set mine eyes upon them for evil, and not for good”: upon the Israelites, because we didn’t keep the commandments. That is the point of the class: wars are here, so seek good and not evil.

“And the Lord God of hosts is he that toucheth the land”: when Iran is touched right now, when Israel is touched, the Lord is involved in all of it. It is by his counsel that the land gets touched.

“and it shall melt”. Amos lived long before missiles were available to move the earth. What melts the land? Thermonuclear bombs, ICBMs, intercontinental ballistic missiles that can go from one continent to another. Right now the Iranians are firing only regular ballistic missiles, and they are destroying parts of the Middle East. “and all that dwell therein shall mourn”.

precepts.why:
“Declaring the end from the beginning”: the Most High God declared the end from the very beginning. “and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”: ancient times, when Adam and Eve walked. From the beginning he planned every war, including the Third World War to come.

That is how we can make a bold statement: God is behind the Israelis doing what they do in the US government, and behind the Iranians spending twenty years building huge tunnel systems and storing munitions and advanced rocketry. Interceptor missiles that cost a million dollars or more are fired at drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand. They will not be able to keep up, and God put all of that in these leaders.

“saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. Just as our going into slavery, through Jim Crow and the civil rights era, was his pleasure: we had to learn the lesson.

This is the power we have: understanding that our Father has it covered, and his Son is coming back. Right now we have to rehearse the righteous acts and get right. So when Amos says the Lord touches the land, it is his counsel standing.

Who is the sword? “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”. God wields the wicked as his sword, and the wicked here is the United States. He uses them to bring in the wars we are seeing. “From men which are thy hand”.

So we can’t bug out or get caught up in everything that is going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children maimed, nobody wants to see destruction, but we understand why it is happening and what we have to do, so that when the final war comes we are among those that endure to the end and are saved. We want deliverance.

Jeremiah saw this. “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord”: as Isaiah 46:10 says, his counsel shall stand, so what Jeremiah wrote shall stand. “that he hath taken against Babylon”: not the Babylon of that time, but the same Babylon the Great, the mystery John the Revelator spoke of. “and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the land of the Chaldeans”.

“Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: a flock is a herd, like sheep, and the least is the smallest. Babylon the Great today is Esau, and the flock is Esau: Germany is part of the flock, the United States is part of it, but Israel is the least of the flock. It draws them out to the Middle East: how else do you set up over 27 military bases throughout the Persian Gulf? Since the 1990s Netanyahu has stood before US officials naming the nations the US should go to war with: Iraq, Libya, Iran, Lebanon. He said take out Saddam and it would all stop; Saddam was taken out, and with Al-Qaeda it did not stop. A foreign government is allowed to come to the United States and speak for its agenda, and the greatest of the flock, Babylon, implements it. Then he said a third nation was Libya. Gaddafi, who gave his people free schooling, free health care and a home, and wanted gold as the standard and all Africans to unite, was taken out. Venezuela became someone harboring terrorists, and did the Israeli military go over there? No. The United States sent in elite special forces to kidnap Nicolas Maduro. Trump and the rest are puppets, in the spirit too: they are doing the will of Netanyahu. That is prophecy, and it is the counsel of the Lord: as God hardened Pharaoh’s heart to send his army after Israel at the Red Sea, he puts it in these leaders’ hearts to make their moves. Donald Trump is not being led by himself.

“surely he shall make their habitation desolate with them”: both of them are going to be destroyed. “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved”: the noise is those missiles, boom, and the superheated clouds of dust. Ancient Babylon could move a castle wall with a giant rock in a sling; nobody could move the earth. Today they possess weapons that move the earth. “and the cry is heard among the nations.”

So the land Amos says the Lord touches and melts is touched by these weapons, by his counsel.

sense.text:
“And the Lord said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark”: Noah got his orders from God. In the chapters before he received the orders on how to build it, exactly what to do and how to do it, and he did it faithfully. “for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation”: Noah taught the laws of God and kept them. He was a godly man in an ungodly world.

Over 100,000 Palestinian Arabs have been killed and many more injured, a thousand or more killed in Iran already, and many more to come. If you think that is bad, revisit the flood. God is a God of power and a God of destruction, and this puts a healthy fear in our minds: in that time there were no righteous except the ones who got on the ark.

“Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee by sevens, the male and his female: and of beasts that are not clean by two”. Christians don’t know the Bible: they tell the story that the animals came on two by two, but it doesn’t even say that first: the clean came by sevens. Even the order is kept: not the female and the male, but “the male and his female”. Christianity pushes two by two because they don’t understand the Bible; if they printed seven by seven, people would begin to question and to read the Bible, and they don’t want that. “Of fowls also of the air by sevens”.

precepts.why:
Why did God choose Noah to be delivered with his family, eight people: Noah, his wife, Shem, Ham and Japheth and their wives? “And spared not the old world”: the old world is what we are reading about in Genesis 7. “but saved Noah the eighth person”: the other seven were his wife, his three sons and their wives. “a preacher of righteousness”: Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. “bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”: Noah was not ungodly. Noah was godly; Noah kept the commandments.

That is why the Lord saw him righteous before him in that generation.

sense.text: “And the flood was forty days upon the earth”. The only people who lived were those in the ark, with the clean by sevens and the unclean by two. “and the waters increased, and bare up the ark, and it was lift up above the earth”: with ten or twenty feet of water the ark began to rise. These people had never seen rain like that. People started floating, and before they drowned they were screaming. All of that was mass destruction.

“And the waters prevailed”: prevail means to win. The waters won, meaning God’s counsel won: his plan of destroying everybody and everything prevailed, as he commanded. “and were increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters.”

“And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth”: it kept rising, fast. “and all the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered”: the high hills are like the foothills in Colorado, hundreds of feet high but not quite mountains. Was it done yet? No. “Fifteen cubits upward did the waters prevail; and the mountains were covered.” It kept rising above the mountains, above Everest and Kilimanjaro, until everything was covered. Noah and his family saw that destruction, looking down at people floating in the water and drowning.

“And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beast, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, and every man”. You might say, why would God kill innocent animals? I don’t know and I don’t care. God has a reason for all that destruction, and we don’t have to worry about why these wars are going on. God set it up; it is happening. Let’s keep the commandments, and God is going to deliver us.

“All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was in the dry land, died”: because it was completely covered with water. The springs beneath were broken up and the rain came down from above. He is a master. The people heard Noah tell them they would be destroyed, and that is what we have to do too. “And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground”. God is a God of terror, a God of destruction, a God of purging. This is why we have to get our minds right.

A thermonuclear war is coming, and that destruction will be on another level. Wars are here; seek good and not evil. We want to be, spiritually, those men and women in the ark, not the ones drowning. That whole generation was wicked as hell. So don’t be surprised when you bring the truth out and your family doesn’t listen. Very few are going to be delivered, but thank the Lord, it will be a lot more than eight.

precepts.why:
“And spared not the old world”: God didn’t spare the old world. He killed all flesh, everything. “but saved Noah the eighth person”: why the eighth? A man of God made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first; he was the last person on the ark. That is what a true captain, a true leader, does. Noah got the word: wife, Shem, Ham, Japheth, get your women, let’s go. They didn’t question him; they got on and closed everything up.

“a preacher of righteousness”: this is why men of God have to be strong. We are all sick; we come to the Sabbath because we’re sick. We have evil minds, fighting the sin of the world that is around us all the time, and in our own thoughts. “bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”: Noah’s righteousness, his standing up for God, is what brought the flood in. God is a master: all these wars going on, God is making it all happen.

sense.text:
Was slavery terrible? Yes. Jim Crow, brothers in the diners sprayed with water hoses and set on by German Shepherds, little black girls and boys spit on going to integrated schools into the seventies: it was not a good thing, but it was a just thing with God that happened to us.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves”: the same people Amos and Moses spoke about. To bethink is to remember again. “in the land whither they were carried captives”: we were carried away captive into all these lands. That is why the bishops, deacons and captains go to places like the Solomon Islands where our people are scattered, and brothers go to India and to Russia. Our people are all over the earth and need to hear this truth, so we cannot get bogged down with politics and wars.

“and repent”: the Christian church is not teaching black people, Latino people or Native Americans to repent. To repent we have to learn God’s commandments and his laws; then we can change. Even in the congregation we still battle, and that is why you need the Sabbath and the new moon, and brothers and sisters who will correct you in righteousness. “and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives”: we have to repent and make supplication to our God in this land.

“saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”. The Christian church has not taught our people that we have sinned, because they say Jesus did away with sin, and if you just believe in your heart and find a good Christian church you’re good. Meanwhile there is homosexuality, infidelity, and remarriage on irreconcilable differences in the Christian church. We are not the Christian church.

“And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies”: the twelve tribes of Israel must return to God and to his Son with all our mind and all our soul, in the land of our enemies. You have to know you have enemies in the lands you were taken to.

We all want mercy. While we see all the destruction, girls’ schools and volleyball teams blown up, ballistic missiles detonating, hypersonic missiles that cannot be shot down in the days, weeks, months and years to come, God is bringing in war, and it is going to get worse. That should give us more reason to repent.

“He that covereth his sins shall not prosper”: men and women, the Israelites. “but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” That is the mercy: if we are in sin we have to confess and forsake, and we are given a dispensation of time. Every one of us is sick. I’m sick, you’re sick, we’re sick: the whole head, all of us.

“Happy is the man that feareth alway”: we have to fear God, and that is when we get what we read in Proverbs 3:1-5. “but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief”: and mischief leads to destruction. Repent, and stand up in these last days.
